history.dynasty: Unverified — present structure dated to the 17th century; major renovation completed around 2021
history.summary: Tara Tarini Temple is one of the four principal Adi Shakti Peethas of India (alongside Kalighat, Kamakhya and Vimala at Puri) and is venerated as the Sthana (Breast) Peetha, where Sati's breasts are believed to have fallen. The twin goddesses Tara and Tarini are worshipped as two ancient stone formations (not conventional sculpted idols), adorned with gold and silver, with brass Chalanti Pratima images between them. Tradition holds the goddess was the chief deity of the Kalinga kingdom's rulers, and most households in southern Odisha keep her as their presiding deity. The present structure is dated to the 17th century; 999 steps lead up Kumari (Purnagiri) Hill, and a ropeway is also available. A comprehensively renovated temple complex in traditional Odia style was inaugurated by Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik in 2021.

name: Tara Tarini Temple
town_description: The temple stands atop Kumari Hill on the bank of the Rushikulya river near Purushottampur, a town in Ganjam district of southern Odisha, about 28–32 km from Berhampur (Brahmapur). Berhampur, the 'Silk City' of Odisha, is the largest city of southern Odisha and the region's commercial hub. The temple sits amid scenic hills overlooking the Rushikulya valley, and is reached by road from Berhampur or by the ropeway from the base.
